title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 32
paragraphs: These mentioned were the greatest of the nations arrayed by Mardonius — the most renowned and of greatest consideration. But in his army were also men of various other nations mixed in: Phrygians, Thracians, Mysians, Paionians, and the rest, including some Ethiopians, and of the Egyptians those called the Hermotybians and Calasirians, armed with knives, who alone of the Egyptians are warriors. These men, while still at Phaleron, he had caused to disembark from the ships where they had served as marines; for the Egyptians had not been appointed to serve in the land-army that came with Xerxes to Athens. There were 300,000 barbarians, as has been said before; but of the Greeks who were allies of Mardonius, no one knows the number, for they were not counted; by conjecture I judge they were assembled to the number of 50,000. These drawn up side by side were on foot, and the cavalry was stationed apart from them as a separate body.
